references.text: In [ref:Matt 21:12-13|Matthew 21:12-13], a similar temple cleansing is described where Jesus drove out those who were selling and buying in the temple, overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of the dove sellers, and called the temple a house of prayer.

[ref:Mark 11:15-17|Mark 11:15-17] tells of Jesus' cleansing of the temple where he drove out those who were selling and buying, overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of the dove sellers, and quoted Isaiah that the temple should be a house of prayer.
[ref:Luk 19:45-46|Luke 19:45-46] describes Jesus' cleansing of the temple, where he drove out those who were conducting business there and declared that his house should be a house of prayer.
[ref:Mal 3:1-3|Malachi 3:1-3] prophesies that the Lord will suddenly come to his temple and purify the sons of Levi. Jesus' action in cleansing the temple is seen as a fulfillment of this prophecy.
[ref:Sak 14:21|Zechariah 14:21] prophesies that there shall no longer be any merchant in the house of the Lord on that day, which Jesus' temple cleansing points to as an eschatological act.
[ref:Sal 69:10|Psalm 69:10] – "Zeal for your house has consumed me" – is quoted in John 2:17 as the disciples' reflection on Jesus' powerful action of driving out the merchants from the temple.

In [ref:Jes 56:7|Isaiah 56:7], the temple is called "a house of prayer for all peoples", a prophecy that provides background for why commercial activity in the temple was a desecration of its holy purpose.
In [ref:4 Mos 25:7-8|Numbers 25:7-8], Phinehas showed zeal for God by intervening with physical action, a parallel to Jesus' zealous act of cleansing the temple with a whip.
